correctness.rationale: A connected spanning active-edge graph makes all polar vertex potentials integral, justifying exact Ehrhart-degree interpolation. The p-part range decomposition is bijective and proves the integer lattice count. Exact rational Newton interpolation exhausts 42 unordered classes with d<=12 and seven classes with d=13. The unique negative coefficient is c1(7,7)=-7184/715; all other coefficients in that vector and all coefficients in other classes are positive. The included checker regenerates all 49 vectors and verifies 48 direct small potential counts, leading coefficient, and reciprocity. All nontrivial computations are reproducible from packaged files; no infinite classification is inferred.

originality.rationale: The closest primary full text (Konoike 2025 Section 4, Example 4.3 and table) concerns the same graph polars but different magic-basis signs; its example K_{3,7} has strictly positive ordinary coefficients. Its table does not imply the unique ordinary first-failure K_{7,7} at dimension 13. The recent Ohsugi–Tsuchiya paper targets stated positive subfamilies and cycles, and 2019 Higashitani–Jochemko–Michałek treats nonpolar originals. Published records and graph-potential synonyms were searched for this exact coefficient and threshold without an established encompassing result. Priority remains provisional because the October 2026 full text was unavailable.
residual_risks: Full text of arxiv:2610.06419 could not be inspected, so a mathematically equivalent corollary in that paper cannot be ruled out.
A differently named graph-Lipschitz or polar counting-table calculation not indexed under the searched terms may predate this result.
Automated exact-arithmetic verification and self-review are not independent research priority certification.

value.rationale: The first ordinary-Ehrhart-positivity failure is a mathematically natural sharp boundary for a canonical reflexive graph-polar family already studied for stronger magic positivity. The theorem answers the minimum dimension and characterizes its unique graph-class obstruction, not merely another isolated counterexample. The all-parameter lattice-point formula also supplies an exact volume and reproducible approach to further coefficient-sign questions.
